phase_name: Canonical Report Finalization Recovery and Push-Semantics Repair
summary: Investigated and repaired a lifecycle-integrity incident: Phase 137F's closure used pcae task complete instead of pcae task finish / pcae phase complete, so .pcae/phase-completion-metadata.json and the canonical phase report were never generated for 137F, yet pcae commit implementation and pcae push both proceeded because neither gates on the canonical report matching the most recently completed phase -- only on that report's own internal schema completeness, which a stale prior-phase report still satisfied. Reproduced the defect directly with fresh fixtures. Repaired assess_push_readiness() (src/pcae/commands/push.py) with a new _detect_phase_report_gap() check that fails closed when the latest canonical report is absent or names a phase other than the most recently completed phase task. Disambiguated pcae push (mutating) from pcae push check (read-only) via corrected CLI help text and an explicit EXECUTING REAL PUSH banner before pcae push runs git push. Recovered the canonical Phase 137F report through the governed lifecycle (pcae phase-report create with explicit phase-id, bypassing active-task identity precedence), corrected .pcae/phase-completion-metadata.json to accurately describe Phase 137F, and explicitly distinguished the original finalization outcome (no report, no notification) from the delayed 137F.1 recovery notification that was actually sent. The Phase 137F VERIFIED verdict is unchanged.
tests_added_or_updated: Added tests/test_push_phase_report_identity_137f1.py (9 tests): missing canonical report blocks push after idle closure, stale prior-phase report blocks push, matching report does not block push, in-progress phase is not blocked, no completed phase task is not blocked, malformed latest.json blocks push, bare pcae push prints the mutating banner, pcae push check never prints it, and pcae push/push check help text discloses their own semantics.
